title: Spark 100-player fleet produced only 2 verified sessions at concurrency 4
body:
A live pure Spark fleet was run from clean build `f7753cd0e775a5888739fefd3c9194b55e41f335` with 100 fresh overworld seeds (`9200`–`9299`), `--no-resume`, `--max-retries 0`, and concurrency 4. The exact Codex CLI was `0.146.0`, and the required three-player Spark admission canary passed 3/3 at concurrency 1.

The 100-player wave produced only 2 evidence-verified sessions (seeds `9200` and `9207`) and 98 failed slots. Of the failures, 96 were exit 43 `strict stream rejected`; seeds `9201` and `9202` were exit 5 malformed reports missing the required Bugs/design-flaws section. There were no technical timeouts, retries, or build-drift failures. Only 2% of the requested cohort yielded usable gameplay evidence.

This is not a game finding: both valid sessions completed Wolf-Winter, rated clarity and enjoyment 4/5, and reported no bugs. It is a fleet reliability finding that prevents a volume cohort from producing trustworthy evidence. Investigate whether concurrency-4 transport/client behavior or Spark output handling causes the strict-stream rejects, preserve a bounded rejection reason per slot, and add a small regression/control proving the mass-fleet lane can sustain verified sessions before spending another 100-player cohort.

Evidence: fleet `spark-100-20260830`, summary and manifest in the referenced ignored artifacts; admission receipt `spark-admission-20260830`.

evidence.summary: 100 Spark players yielded 2 verified and 98 failed slots; 96 strict-stream rejects and 2 malformed interviews
